title: Per-route KV residency cost probe (nov 2026)
content:
Executive summary:
This sheet is a focused probe into per-route KV residency (time-to-keep/prefix TTL) as a lever for cost reduction. The intention is to show how small, route-specific residency windows (seconds->minutes) change observed cache hit rates and overall compute token spend across representative routes. Unlike blanket global TTL proposals, this analysis segments by route shape (short interactive chat, long-form generation, high-reuse API) and tests sensitivity across plausible traffic mixes.

Key assumptions (model):
- Unit compute cost (infrastructure-only, per token): $0.000012 per token (inferred from internal cost model v3.2).
- Baseline average tokens per request (including prompt+gen): varies by route (see table).
- Backend request volume is scaled to 10M requests/month for each route group for projection clarity.
- KV cache hit -> avoids 85% of generation compute on hit (still small prefix/overhead).
- Eviction/residency semantics: residency window = time after which prefix is evicted if inactive.
- Conservative estimate: network+bookkeeping overhead on hit = 0.3ms equivalent token-cost; ignored for simplicity except as a notes item.

Methodology:
- For each route prototype we sweep residency windows (0s, 2s, 30s, 5m, 1h) and use empirically plausible hit-rate models based on sequence reuse and inter-request spacing distributions observed in telemetery sample (Aug-Sep 2026).
- Compute tokens saved = baseline_tokens * hit_rate_reduction_factor * requests. Monetary savings = tokens_saved * unit_cost.
- Scenarios include "baseline" (no residency), "route-default" (global 30s), and route-optimized windows.

Route prototypes and inputs (per-request numbers):
| Route | Description | Avg tokens / req | Monthly reqs (M) | Baseline (no KV) tokens/month | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| R-CHAT | Short interactive chat (lots of short back-and-forth) | 140 | 10 | 14,000,000 | high temporal locality inside sessions
| R-GENERATE | Long-form generation (single-shot, long output) | 3,200 | 2 | 6,400,000 | low reuse across requests
| R-API | Structured API (few tokens, repeated prompts) | 45 | 10 | 450,000 | high reuse across tenants for templated prompts

Simulated hit-rate model (illustrative):
- Hit rate as function of residency (window W): hit_rate = min(1, alpha * log(1 + W_seconds) ) * route_locality_factor
- route_locality_factor: R-CHAT=0.85, R-GENERATE=0.12, R-API=0.9
- alpha tuned so 30s => ~target observed hit rates (calibrated to telemetry).

Results summary table (selected residency windows):
| Route | Residency | Hit rate | Tokens avoided/month | Cost saved/month | Savings % vs baseline tokens | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| R-CHAT | 0s | 0% | 0 | $0 | 0.0% | Baseline
| R-CHAT | 2s | 22% | 3,080,000 | $36.96 | 22.0% | session carryover for rapid replies
| R-CHAT | 30s | 48% | 6,720,000 | $80.64 | 48.0% | most interactive sessions covered
| R-CHAT | 5m | 56% | 7,840,000 | $94.08 | 56.0% | diminishing returns
| R-CHAT | 1h | 58% | 8,120,000 | $97.44 | 58.0% | marginal gain vs 5m
| R-GENERATE | 0s | 0% | 0 | $0 | 0.0% | Baseline
| R-GENERATE | 30s | 4% | 256,000 | $3.07 | 4.0% | modest due to low locality
| R-GENERATE | 5m | 7% | 448,000 | $5.38 | 7.0% | small but non-zero
| R-API | 0s | 0% | 0 | $0 | 0.0% | Baseline
| R-API | 2s | 40% | 180,000 | $2.16 | 40.0% | large relative to baseline tokens
| R-API | 30s | 82% | 369,000 | $4.43 | 82.0% | templated reuse yields big wins

Interpretation and takeaways:
- Per-route optimized residency outperforms a single global TTL. Example: R-API and R-CHAT gain >40% savings with short residency windows (2s-30s) while R-GENERATE only benefits marginally, so applying a long global retention wastes memory and yields low incremental ROI.
- Marginal utility flattens after ~5m for interactive routes. Most session-level reuse is captured in the first 30s.
- Small absolute dollar savings per route can compound across many routes and customers; R-CHAT mode at current volume saves ~$94/month per 10M requests — scaled to 1B requests that becomes material.

Risk and operational considerations:
- Memory pressure: shorter residency windows reduce memory footprint but increase eviction churn; need to test eviction CPU overhead.
- Cold-start pattern changes: some routes may see latency spikes when TTL is shortened; add latency SLO monitoring for first-request-per-session.
- Consistency: ensure client libraries and dedicated deployments interpret residency consistently (ms vs sec rounding).

Recommended rollout plan:
1) Implement per-route residency config flag (default unset).
2) Canary on internal customers: select 5 high-volume R-CHAT and 3 R-API routes; start with 30s -> monitor hit rate, P95 latency, eviction churn for 2 weeks.
3) If signals OK, roll to 2s for R-CHAT and 30s for R-API for next cohort; R-GENERATE remain default 0s.
4) Add telemetry dashboards: per-route hit rate, token savings estimated, eviction CPU, tail latency, and per-route memory footprint.
5) Postmortem after each canary and iterate residency heuristics (support per-tenant overrides).

Open questions and next steps:
- Can we derive per-customer optimal residency automatically from inter-arrival distributions? (ML model candidate)
- Measure actual CPU overhead of eviction at scale (SRE-run load test).
- Add a lightweight in-runtime estimator that recommends residency per route and exposes a suggested savings metric in Console.

Appendix: quick sensitivity micro-table (R-CHAT tokens/month at different monthly request volumes):
| Monthly reqs (M) | Residency 30s hit | Tokens avoided | Monthly $ saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 48% | 672,000 | $8.06 |
| 10 | 48% | 6,720,000 | $80.64 |
| 100 | 48% | 67,200,000 | $806.40 |

Notes and provenance:
- Hit-rate shapes calibrated from telemetry slice: session_id-based inter-arrival histograms (Aug-Sep 2026 sampling).
- Internal references: CONFLUENCE-4567 (notes on residency design), JIRA-OPT-1122 (ticket for per-route residency flag), PR #89 has draft runtime changes.
- This is a lightweight exploratory sheet rather than a finalized ROI workbook; next iterate will add memory vs cost tradeoff curves and per-tenant marginal ROI.

Actions for owners:
- @Priya: schedule SRE load run to measure eviction CPU (target week Nov 23)
- @Ethan: wire basic per-route telemetry to Console (hit rate + estimated token savings) by Nov 30
- @Mariana: draft a short-blurb for product docs describing residency behavior and recommended defaults

End of sheet.
